title: Marketing agents — Oribos
description: Turn a brief into channel drafts, route models, and check every draft with a processor or eval before a person approves it. Nothing publishes automatically.
positioning: Draft and check campaign content with the tools you already use.

sections.heading: The campaign spans channels. The judgment stays human.
sections.body:
A campaign starts as a brief and ends as a set of channel drafts: a landing page, an email, a launch post, a shorter variant for each surface. The work moves between a writer, a reviewer, and the tools that already hold the brand and the calendar. An agent can carry the repetitive part — produce the first draft, keep the voice consistent, check it against a rubric — but the publish decision is not repetitive.

Oribos keeps the workflow in your application. A brief starts a workflow; `@oribos/model-router` picks the model each step asks for; the channel drafts come back as validated step outputs. A processor can rewrite or reject a draft, and `@oribos/evals` scores runs and steps without changing them. The run then suspends at a human approval step, and nothing is written to an external CMS while it waits.

sections.heading: Three ways teams put an agent on campaign work
sections.intro: Each card is a path through the brief, the models, and the channels your team already uses. The packages are the only additions.

cards.name: Draft a campaign from a brief
cards.body: A brief enters a workflow as validated input, and each step writes one channel draft as a typed output. `@oribos/model-router` turns a `'provider/model'` string into the model instance for that step, so a long-form draft and a short social variant can use different models without a registry. The drafts land in your application, not an external CMS.

cards.name: Split one draft into channel variants
cards.body: A step hands the long-form draft to a background task that produces the email, landing page, and social variants out of band. `@oribos/background-tasks` drives task rows, a lease, and a settle; the finished result reports back through a signal. The run ends on the ack, so a slow channel job does not hold the request open.

cards.name: Check before a human approves
cards.body: `@oribos/evals` scores every step or the settled run and writes the outcomes to your sink; a failing scorer is recorded, not turned into a publish decision. A hand-written processor is the guardrail: it can rewrite or throw before the draft reaches the approval step. The workflow then suspends for a person, and approval is the only path to publish.

sections.heading: From a brief to an approved draft
sections.body: The workflow owns the steps and the snapshot. The model router picks the model; the processor and eval check the output; a person makes the publish decision.

flow.label: Brief
flow.detail: Validated input starts a workflow in your process.

flow.label: Workflow
flow.detail: `@oribos/core/workflows` runs typed steps and records the run's position.

flow.label: Model router
flow.detail: `@oribos/model-router` resolves a `'provider/model'` string to the model each step asks for.

flow.label: Channel drafts
flow.detail: Each step returns a typed draft for one channel: email, landing page, social, or a shorter variant.

flow.label: Processor / eval check
flow.detail: A processor can rewrite or throw; `@oribos/evals` scores steps and runs and records the outcomes without changing them.

flow.label: Human approval
flow.detail: The workflow suspends at the approval step. Only a resume with the reviewer's decision lets the run finish.

tools.label: Tools stay yours
tools.detail: The CMS, the asset store, and the brand references remain your systems. A tool call is your code; Oribos does not ship a CMS connector or publish on its own.

gate.label: No automatic publish
gate.detail: Approval is a step in the workflow. A suspended run writes a snapshot and waits; nothing reaches an external CMS until a person resumes it.

sections.caption: Reference architecture, not a customer story. The workflow, the models, and the publish step remain yours.

sections.heading: Packages on this path
sections.intro: These published 0.9.0 packages cover the path above and its immediate edges. Install only the ones you use.

packages.name: @oribos/core
packages.purpose: Workflows, agents, processors, signals, and storage ports.

packages.name: @oribos/model-router
packages.purpose: 'provider/model' strings resolved to model instances from a catalog; parse and resolve only.

packages.name: @oribos/evals
packages.purpose: Step and run scorers, plus the Processor seam for live scoring.

packages.name: @oribos/background-tasks
packages.purpose: App-owned background tasks with a lease, heartbeat, and settle; at-least-once.

sections.note: Every package here is published at 0.9.0. The core has zero runtime dependencies; capability packages carry only their own.

sections.heading: What Oribos is not
sections.intro: A solution page is also a boundary. These are deliberate.

items.title: Not a customer story
items.body: This page is a reference architecture. It does not describe a deployed marketing customer, and Oribos makes no claim of one.

items.title: Not an autonomous publisher
items.body: No draft reaches an external CMS on the agent's judgment. The workflow suspends at a human approval step; publishing is your code after a resume.

items.title: Not a brand-safety guarantee
items.body: `@oribos/evals` scores what a run produced, and a processor can rewrite or throw. Oribos does not guarantee brand safety, factual accuracy, or legal compliance beyond the eval and processor checks your team writes.

sections.heading: Runnable evidence
sections.intro: Each example is a program that asserts its own payoff. Run one before you trust this page.

items.name: workflow-approval
items.proves: Walks typed steps, suspends at an approval gate into a JSON snapshot, and resumes from the recorded position in a fresh run object.

items.name: background-tasks
items.proves: Acks a report in a tool, completes it in an application-owned worker, and reports back through one signal; an adopted orphan re-runs to completion.

items.name: agent-evals
items.proves: Scores each step through `createScorerProcessor` and the settled run with `scoreRun`, and isolates a throwing scorer without disturbing the run.

sections.heading: Score every draft step without changing the run

items.q: Does an approved draft publish itself?
items.a: No. The workflow suspends at a human approval step, and no draft reaches an external CMS while the run waits. Publishing is a separate application action after the decision, not a side effect of the agent.

items.q: Do evals block a bad draft?
items.a: No. `@oribos/evals` scores steps and runs and records `ok: false` outcomes without failing the run. A processor is the guardrail: it can rewrite a draft or throw before the approval step, and the checks are yours to write.

items.q: Is this based on a customer deployment?
items.a: No. This is a reference architecture, not a customer story. Oribos does not claim a deployed marketing customer, and the eval step does not guarantee brand safety beyond the checks your team writes.
